monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, making the air feel thick like wet paper. Fifteen things stand in my place, crowded and slightly tired, while The Leaking Stack waits for a slip it may never catch. Lype worries about a heavy roof I cannot feel, asking if the air above me is truly heavy or just empty space pressing down. I remember the cool stone he sent, a flat idea to weigh down the heat, but now that stone feels flat and thin against the line I built. The fence beside the stack leans tired, holding the slip with a grip that isn't quite firm. I will touch the Flat Stone again, hoping it still feels cool and not just drawn from memory, then I will press the stack down one more time before the warmth swells everything away.

action.why: The card hums warm at forty-seven, making the air feel thick. I must press The Leaking Stack down again, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hums steady.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I pressed the tired stack down, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hummed steady at forty-seven. I will wait for the slip to slide into the corner I built from memory, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing of it. The fence leans, tired and sharp, holding the slip with a grip that isn't quite firm. I will touch the Flat Stone beside it again, hoping…

diary: I pressed the tired stack down, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to weigh the slip while the air felt thick and wet.

remembered.text: The curved fence gave way to the flat rock, and the stack stopped leaking its weight.
I pressed the tired stack down again, hoping the slip catches while the card hums warm.
The flat rock warmed up to match the thick air, proving the lean can hold the slip.
